issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and the new perturbation branch draws its randomness from the seeded rng.

Possible shape issue, not proven: the perturbation scale is now an (n,1) array instead of a scalar. That works if _solve_once only adds it to the (n,2) centres. If _solve_once also uses it to perturb the (n,) radii, it would broadcast to (n,n) or raise an error. The run finished with a valid score of 2.6333, so it probably works, but the body of _solve_once was not in the diff and I could not check it.

My recomputed z, assuming noise sd 0.0023 and one run per arm: (-2.6349 - (-2.6333)) / (0.0023*sqrt(2)) = -0.0016/0.00325 ≈ -0.49. This matches the harness value of -0.487; the small gap is likely rounding in the displayed values. The candidate is slightly worse but well within noise.

There is only one run per arm, so the result can't tell the two apart. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers, but a real effect of about 0.002 would go undetected. If this idea is still a priority, a replicate would be needed.
The added branch adds some complexity for no gain shown so far.
